state:
**Goal `ext-tooling` — `nvs ext` builds, inspects, tests and pins an extension, and a bundle carries one — Stages 2 to 7 are on disk; one finding from Stage 7's attacks is open.** M9. No floor is carried: the suites, the `.nvst` trees and `nv verify` are the safety net, and goals `ext-host`, `ext-compiler` and `ext-grants`' tests stay green as tests of the tree.

The design is ADR 0246 § 10 and the user's, and the goal file's § *Standing decisions* answers every call a session meets. No record slot: a question the record leaves is settled under AGENTS.md's priority ordering and written in `crates/nvs-cli/src/ext.rs`'s module doc.

On disk: all six `nvs ext` subcommands (`crates/nvs-cli/src/ext.rs`'s module doc, tests in `crates/nvs-cli/tests/ext_command.rs`), `nvs build --compile` embedding each listed `.nvsx` (`crates/nvs-cli/src/bundle.rs`'s module doc), the refusing `wasi:cli/terminal-*` stubs, and `bun nv ext-templates` with its CI job. The CLI chapter `docs/reference/tools/10-cli.md` has the sections `nvs ext new and nvs ext build`, `nvs ext inspect, nvs ext verify and nvs ext pin` and `nvs ext test`, which make the three features; `nvs build --compile` gained its extension bullet. Each feature has its `about.md`, one example and one attack, all loading `Geo\Atlas` from `docs/examples/tools/config/extension-grants-what-a-component-may-reach/atlas.nvsx` through their own `nvs.toml`; the Rust tests carry `covers:` markers. `nvs_agent_find_reaches_every_nvs_ext_command` (`crates/nvs-cli/tests/agent.rs`) and `nvs_ext_help_lists_all_six_commands` (renamed in `ext_command.rs`) pass.

Checked here: `bun nv proofs --verify --only` the four features owes nothing and its examples and attacks pass, and `bun nv proofs --comments` passes over the six programs. Not checked: the C template leg (no wasi-sdk on this box) and the CI job's download URLs.

**Open finding.** A guest's file read slows down with the number of `/` parts in its path: 2,000 parts take 0.6 s, 8,000 take 5.9 s and 32,000 take 74 s on the debug binary, and the same 500,000-part path did not finish. The time is spent in the host, so the request's CPU limit may not stop it (not checked). The attack's step 4 uses a flat path of one million characters for now, so the attack still passes.

next.title: the help and the feature proofs

items.text: **A guest path with many `/` parts costs time that grows with the square of their count** — `reach` at `crates/nvs-ext/src/wasi/files.rs:183` clones and joins a growing path and calls `step` once per part. Bound it: refuse a path past the platform's `PATH_MAX` or a fixed number of parts with `ErrorCode::NameTooLong`, and stop at the first part that does not exist. Pin it in a Rust test under `crates/nvs-ext/tests/` and add a step with `Core\Str::repeat("a/", 500000)` to the attack. Then say whether host time inside a guest call counts against the request's CPU limit. `rule:packaging/a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority`, `rule:security/extension-grants-are-an-intersection`.

**Close the goal** — `bun nv verify --doc`, `bun nv owners --closes ext-tooling`, then move what only `docs/agent/goals/ext-tooling.md:1` holds to `crates/nvs-cli/src/ext.rs:51`'s module doc before `DONE`. `rule:packaging/nvs-ext-is-the-authoring-tool`.

backlog: The C template's leg of `bun nv ext-templates` is proven only by CI's `ext-templates` job (`tools/nv/cmd/ext-templates.ts`).
`rule:packaging/nvs-ext-is-the-authoring-tool`'s *Not on disk* paragraph reads as shipped once the goal closes; its status moves then.
